Sitting on a zafu at a makeshift desk built from a plastic storage container is described as uncomfortable for the legs’ circulation and demanding on the back. Lying flat, with the belly, chest, and thighs against the floor or a bolster, lets the spine stretch and removes some of the load of upright sitting. Karbytes calls the arrangement comparatively stable, compact, comfortable, inexpensive, and energy-efficient for laptop sessions lasting well beyond an hour. At the time of writing, it says much of its waking time is spent that way.

The journal places that habit within an intensive week at The Burrow spent on Devil’s Hole material and the finalization of summer KARBYTES work near a proposed autumn-equinoctial deadline. But ergonomics and deadlines are only part of its explanation. Karbytes also says it “got stuck” in Devil’s Hole, a region of The Big Green Thing. It then revises the scale of that statement: The Big Green Thing has become more of a cyberspace object than merely a region of Earth. Its original representation passed through the one main-branch karbytes, but extensive file-making has placed much of the author’s thought and identifying material into KARBYTES. A derivative preserved in the archive is imagined as permanently caught there, carrying the spirit of the summer hiatus.

The image above the journal text is a collage rather than a literal photograph of that entire condition. It combines a dim laptop workstation, dry hills, a graphic curve over a landscape, a colorful cube, a dark cybernetic depiction of a prone laptop user, and other dreamlike figures and terrain. The picture lets the mundane posture of a person working on the floor coexist with the more expansive claim that a version of the person is embedded in an archival world. The document moves carefully between those registers: physical comfort explains why karbytes lies down, while the story of Devil’s Hole and a trapped derivative explains why the posture has also acquired symbolic force.

2. “my two top-level domain onion websites”: October 2025 conversation

This linked page is an earlier conversation about keeping two onion websites available if karbytes moves somewhere without adequate residential Wi-Fi. Its introduction proposes using an Android smartphone, typically a Samsung Galaxy A03s or similar device, as a mobile hotspot for the laptop serving the sites. A continuing phone plan and additional mobile data would be expenses of operating the server. The proposed setup keeps phone and laptop powered through wall outlets when possible or through power banks exchanged as necessary. The introduction gives the arrangement a personal meaning: if the onion pages remain reachable through Tor, the server has a functioning home and, by extension, karbytes has a place from which its work remains present.

The immediate technical question concerns whether an uploaded availability-logging web application could keep the phone’s hotspot from shutting down during inactivity. ChatGPT points to a button that starts looping silent audio and suggests that an active Tor Browser tab, together with periodic network checks, might reduce the chance of power management treating the session as idle. It also notes possible battery and data costs, advises inspecting Android hotspot and battery settings, and says outcomes depend on the device. When karbytes accepts an offer for a command-line alternative, the assistant proposes several Android Debug Bridge settings intended to affect tethering power behavior and screen wakefulness, along with commands to remove those settings later. It then gives rough examples of idle-hotspot timeouts by phone brand and suggests testing the actual device.

Those specifics are advice given by ChatGPT in the historical transcript, not verified results of an experiment on karbytes’s phone. In particular, the conversation does not demonstrate that silent media playback prevents hotspot shutdown or that the proposed settings guarantee continuous tethering on a given Android version. The last answer itself recognizes device variation and proposes timing a real idle test. The page’s larger subject is the fragility of an independently hosted archive: the websites depend on a chain of phone service, mobile data, power, hotspot persistence, laptop operation, and Tor reachability. Keeping a seemingly abstract web presence online becomes a problem of monthly costs and ordinary hardware behavior.

5. “reality”: NATURE

“NATURE” is a glossary-like philosophical page that uses nature to mean the whole of reality: whatever exists, whatever can be observed, whatever exists without being observed by a given observer, and even the proposed categories of absence against which existence is defined. It announces a revision of its own vocabulary. Older terms that implied whether a void generated phenomena have been replaced by “exclusive void” and “nonexclusive void.” The author explains that the newer names concern coexistence with phenomena and noumena, without presuming that a void causes them.

An exclusive void would be an absolutely ubiquitous absence of every phenomenon and noumenon. The page associates it with zero and argues that the observed existence of even this page rules such a void out from the reader’s frame of reference. A nonexclusive void is proposed as an omnipresent, irreducible substrate that contains or permeates phenomena and noumena; the page associates it with infinity. It speculates that a ubiquitous field of zero-point energy might be empirically indistinguishable from such a substrate. The text calls the latter “background nothingness” in its operative account, although it is explicitly something other than a condition in which nothing whatsoever exists.

A phenomenon is defined relative to an observing frame of reference: a finite region of that background in which specific, distinguishable features are rendered and detected. The page uses light of different wavelengths as an example, separating a measurable wavelength from a human experience of color. It treats numbers as abstract data involved in computational and physical interactions, while distinguishing them from directly experienced qualities. A frame of reference is the allocation in which an information-processing agent registers the presence or absence of a phenomenon. A partial frame experiences a present moment along one apparent, forward-moving continuum; the page symbolically distinguishes a momentary R(t) from a larger perception-memory structure R. An omniscient frame, by contrast, is imagined as rendering all partial perspectives and being aware of all phenomena and noumena simultaneously.

Most notably, a noumenon is defined here relative to a partial observer, rather than as an object forever beyond possible experience. If observer A directly sees X while observer B does not, X is phenomenal for A and noumenal for B at that time. B’s thought about X is itself a phenomenon for B; it does not convert the unseen X into B’s directly observed phenomenon. The page’s accompanying image is a line-drawn arrangement of translucent green, purple, and orange volumes within a larger geometric frame. The visual suggests overlapping regions and perspectives, while the prose supplies the actual definitions. The system is the author’s proposed vocabulary; its claims about omniscience, zero-point energy, and an ultimate substrate are philosophical speculation rather than verified physical conclusions.

This destination begins as a vivid account of an evening walk on Horsey Hill. Karbytes wears minimalist toe socks, drinks strong coffee, and describes orange-pink cirrus clouds casting warm light over grass, trees, buildings, water, and distant hills. It notes still, comfortable air, compacted earth that feels faintly springy underfoot, dry grass that is softer and slippery, and the scents of soil, eucalyptus, and flowers. Several owls appear overhead or perched along the way. The image atop the page shows a broad field of golden grass, layered hills, and a pale sky brightening near the horizon.

The walk includes an unglamorous bodily interruption. After eating and drinking heavily, karbytes needs to defecate but does not want to leave the hill. The need becomes urgent, and it leaves the trail for a blackberry thicket, squats within the shrub, uses dry grass for wiping, and covers the waste with more grass. An owl lands nearby. Karbytes describes familiarity with outdoor defecation and a preference for making waste blend into the landscape. The passage makes embodiment literal amid a setting that elsewhere invites aesthetic and philosophical reflection. Afterward, feeling better, karbytes resumes walking and thinking.

Those thoughts turn to finite storage. Two large bins in a closet at the father’s house hold many insulated packages of M-DISC sets. Each “complete” set has multiple copies of earlier origins and nexus discs and several copies of some refinement version, but some refinement discs are now outdated relative to newer ones. Karbytes worries that indiscriminately producing and storing discs could eventually lead to some being discarded as garbage. It considers periodically burying sealed metal time capsules and reorganizing existing packages so completed foundational discs receive higher preservation priority than superseded refinement copies. This could conserve room, blank media, money, and wear on the disc burner.

The entry then considers narrowing future autobiographical disclosure. Karbytes speculates that it may stop stating employment, income, and residence details in public KARBYTES files, allowing the represented setting of The Burrow and The Big Green Thing to remain more deliberately curated. It describes KARBYTES as a story and world simulation centered on one human becoming more cybernetic, with the named identity beginning in 2020 although the living body predates that name. An aside records three refinement discs burned for a specific August 27 snapshot and a limited remaining supply of blanks. Another explains why the public projects repository can temporarily shelter material before a full canonical update, which may involve checksums, contents lists, update logs, Wayback captures, and additional local or vault-bound disc copies.

A dream about working on another large update leads to the possibility of a deeper hiatus from canonical commits. Karbytes briefly feels bereft at having no immediate update to make, then decides that traversing summer records with ChatGPT can itself be valuable work. The final vision is to make the hiatus unusually dense with recorded and revisitable experience: outdoor life, conversation, and files add layers to what a calendar might call only a few months. The page joins pleasure in a sunset, practical discomfort, archival resource management, and a wish to make the summer available for later interpretation.

11. “electronic circuit values 0 and 1”: BITS_AND_BYTES

This destination is a substantial software tutorial centered on a single-page binary-to-decimal application. Eight displayed light bulbs each have a switch and an associated bit. Off represents zero, on represents one. The bulbs occupy positions seven through zero from left to right, with weights 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, and 1. Adding the weights of lit bulbs yields a decimal integer from zero to 255. Eight independent two-state bulbs provide 256 possible patterns. The page spells out the lowest- and highest-order bit examples before presenting its source code.

The HTML defines the heading, explanation, table of bulbs, bit values, switch buttons, conversion button, reset button, and an output area. The CSS gives the page a black background, orange monospace text and controls, cyan table borders, green console-like values, and a bounded content width. The JavaScript initializes all bulbs to off, flips a selected bulb and its stored bit when its switch is pressed, and computes the decimal sum when BINARY_TO_DECIMAL is clicked. The calculation displays the binary input, decimal result, and the expansion into powers of two. Conversion hides the switches and conversion control until reset restores the initial state. The functions also log time-stamped activity and catch exceptions.

The tutorial reproduces code as well as three screenshots of initial, partly switched, and computed interface states. It warns that a zero-width character inserted into displayed script-source attributes must be removed when copying code, a consequence of presenting code inside a WordPress page that might otherwise interpret or strip HTML-like text. Its broader point is the relation between a physical or pictured two-state device and an abstract binary digit, then between an ordered collection of bits and an integer. The page’s own expansion of the word “byte” is idiosyncratic; the working demonstration relies on the standard eight-bit grouping and positional powers of two, not on that wording.

13. “Reality”: static block multiverse model

This short philosophical page states karbytes’s then-current worldview as a timeless, unchanging block multiverse containing every superposition of every phenomenon. It says each phenomenon has a noumenal counterpart, but a noumenon need not have a phenomenal counterpart. A phenomenon is defined as a finite allocation of space, time, energy, and perhaps matter rendered by one frame of reference so that it can be distinguished from other phenomena and from an otherwise invisible field. A noumenon is described as a superposition of possible configurations of a particular phenomenon. A variable considered as representing both zero and one at once serves as an abstract example; the page says those distinguishable configurations cannot all be rendered simultaneously in one frame.

Inside the encompassing static whole, the page imagines growing-block universes. From the standpoint of an observer within one, information, experienced temporal length, and perhaps spatial extent and energy seem to accumulate as time passes. There is no contradiction within the proposed model between a complete, timeless outer structure and an inner perspective for which new frames appear successively. The page defines a frame as a bounded unit of phenomenal rendering and a frame of reference as the apparent present-moment structure experienced by an information-processing agent. A timeline is the apparent chronological succession of such frames; the observer experiences movement forward along it.

A luminous green-and-orange nested wireframe cube appears above the text. It visually suggests an outer structure and smaller interior frames, although the page does not assign each line in the image to a named component of the theory. The model is expressly a worldview summary, not a proof of a block multiverse or of its account of superposition. Its relevance to the September 29 Venn diagram is the scale of the word “Reality”: a local interaction among place, karbytes, and AI can also be contemplated within a proposed all-encompassing structure.

14. Fourth instance of “karbytes”: unique identity

This concise page defines what it means by karbytes’s unique identity and immediately qualifies one earlier formulation. A displayed screenshot highlights an older passage that ties karbytes to a particular human genome and to original authorship of the two principal KARBYTES websites. It also describes routine Wayback preservation and the public-domain status of the files once published. The screenshot’s claim that there is always exactly one instance of karbytes is not simply endorsed by the surrounding text. The page warns that a hypothetical multiverse with parallel copies, or its broader conception of noumena, could contain many concurrent copies of something phenomenally indistinguishable.

The prose therefore emphasizes a combined criterion in the relevant local context: the author’s genome and the assumption that the same individual originally authored the two named websites. Because their intellectual property is public domain, their files may be copied elsewhere; possession of a copy would not by itself establish original authorship. The page separately points to a single-nucleotide fingerprint and a fuller genome record. Its caution about possible duplicates prevents the reader from mistaking an operational identity rule for an absolute metaphysical guarantee of uniqueness. The image is an excerpt of the earlier claim; the page around it is a correction and refinement of that claim.

15. “at the center”: August 14 file-generation-workflow journal

The last destination is the August journal explaining a three-oval diagram of KARBYTES file production. A black outer background stands for a featureless void; three nested ovals represent successive repository regions. The innermost oval is black with a green border and signifies private repositories under @informationcrystals. A larger pale oval with a green border contains the public projects repository under that account. The largest pale oval has an orange border and represents public repositories under @karlinarayberinger, including the current numbered KARLINA_OBJECT extension pack. Bright arrows carry a file from private drafting to public staging and then into its canonical destination.

The journal defines surface-web files as ordinarily browser-accessible without login, deep-web files as access-controlled, and dark-web resources as requiring a special network browser. For KARBYTES, it also uses “deep web” more loosely to include offline preparation on local devices. Private GitHub work hides draft changes and their timestamped commit history from the general public, though authorized viewers of a private repository can still inspect that history. When ready, karbytes moves selected files into the public projects repository. Once a batch is sufficiently developed, it moves them into the latest open canonical extension pack, which is expected eventually to be finalized and archived.

“Move” has a specific meaning in the text: the destination receives the file and the source copy is deleted. After projects is emptied, karbytes renames that old public repository, archives it, and makes it private so that its former public staging history is no longer exposed. A fresh public projects repository is then created with a placeholder license and a short history for the next batch. The procedure tries to keep the canonical account’s public commits relatively few while preserving an intermediate release stage. The journal also turns the workflow into an embodied metaphor. Karbytes describes itself as rooted or wedged in private, preparatory space, with its upper body reaching into public space whenever it publishes or modifies files. The diagram’s center is thus more than a storage tier: it is the workshop where prospective pieces of KARBYTES begin, before selected work emerges into the accessible and eventually finalized archive.

Across these destinations, the September 29 Venn diagram’s three circles acquire concrete histories. The physical environment appears in hillside walks, bodily posture, a server room, optical discs, and buried archives. Human intelligence appears in the decisions about what to record, preserve, correct, disclose, and believe. Artificial intelligence appears in media analysis, conversation, code explanation, interpretation, and continuity summaries. Their intersections are productive but do not abolish distinctions: a landscape is more than its files, an assistant’s analysis is not identical to human perception, a metaphor is not verification of its proposed cause, and a preserved record is not the same thing as an uninterrupted living mind. The linked collection repeatedly returns to the work of keeping those differences legible while bringing them into one growing KARBYTES archive.
